title: A slower week, and God’s timing
excerpt: A weekly wrap-up, Bueno Matcha, Shin’s birthday, and reflections on Job, calling and God’s timing.

body.text: NGL, i have been procrastinating on my third blog entry cos:

items: While i have countless things i want to write about, i do not want to be posting almost every other day. #creatingscarcity JK
i feel like i will end up in a content drought if i post too much at once. #consistencyiskey

body.text: It is Sunday, and even as i type this, i am still deliberating whether to discuss what went down in church (back-to-back religious content) or do a weekly wrap-up HAHAHA.
SIDE NOTE: big shoutout to <W> coffee and matcha. They have a very nice cafe, and there is a new addition to the menu: the glorious Bueno Matcha.

The blend is insane. i love Kinder Bueno, and when i first got the drink, it was pure green. i was half expecting some brown in there because of the chocolate or syrup, but holy shit, neither the Bueno nor the matcha overpowered the other. i could taste both distinctly, and they worked so well together. 5/5 drink.

Anyway, i had a slower week, and tbf, i feel like i deserved the change of pace. October was terribly hectic: meetings with SSIA and Web Summit, SWITCH, Container Days, two hackathons and a demo day. There were so many events back to back, and it was a definite ramp-up from the previous few months, when tech and AI events were more sporadic and i could pace myself and plan my rest.

i started Monday with a short hike through Rifle Range and Bukit Timah, did some implementation work with Singpass on Tuesday (very good learning experience ngl), squeezed in a sweet 5 + 2 km run on Wednesday, and attended an AI seminar on Thursday (shoutout to the folks at SGInnovate).
Friday finally brought a slower pace, and i got to grab some ice cream to round off the workweek. Thank you, Microsoft, for taking Outlook down. i needed the rest ngl.

Saturday was p fun. i started the day with a cell group meeting, went for a steamboat dinner with my friends to celebrate Shin’s 27th birthday (happy birthday, Shin, you are old!), then headed to Unfiltered’s rebrand activation. Bye bye to Unfiltered Presents.
Alongside all of that, i also had some rather fruitful thoughts about religion this week. Cell, in particular, left me with a couple of things to think about.
1. Train of thought numero uno: our relationship with God is not a transaction
i disagree with the way Eliphaz explains Job’s suffering. My dear brother in Christ, have some sympathy for my man Job fr, or some self-awareness at least HAHA.

“Consider now: Who, being innocent, has ever perished?
Where were the upright ever destroyed?
As I have observed, those who plow evil
and those who sow trouble reap it.”
— Job 4:7–8, NIV.
Eliphaz does kinda suffer from tunnel vision fr. He seems so convinced that suffering must be the result of wrongdoing that he assumes Job must have done something to deserve it.

But doing good does not guarantee a life free from suffering. We see this all the time irl: bad things DO happen to good people. Think of Jesus, who was righteous and without sin, yet still suffered so deeply.
That also got me thinking about how easily we can turn our relationship with God into a transaction, as though doing enough good should guarantee that things go our way.
i do not think we can say stuff like, “Oh, i did three good deeds today. That should cover the two bad things i did yesterday, so i should still be in God’s good books.”
Or, even worse, start assigning points to our sins and good deeds: helping an old man cross the road, +1 point; helping the needy, +2 points; stealing a pack of Pokémon cards, −1 point, etc etc.
Who are we to assume that God works according to our own scoring system? i think we would be foolish to believe we can game our way into heaven fr HAHA.
Good works matter, but salvation is not something we earn by keeping our score above zero. That is where grace comes in.
Ephesians 2:8–10, NIV.
2. God’s timing, and learning to trust it
The other thing i have been thinking about is trusting God’s purpose and timing. There were four major points that stuck with me:
1. i am called for God’s purpose, not mine.
“For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.”
— Ephesians 2:10, NIV.
kai: This can be understood as a reminder to look beyond personal plans and ambitions, and pay attention to what God is calling you to do.
2. Your calling is permanent; your vocation is not.
“for God’s gifts and his call are irrevocable.”
— Romans 11:29, NIV.

kai: Paul is speaking about God’s faithfulness to Israel here, so applying this verse to an individual’s vocation is a personal reflection. The distinction you are drawing is between living for God’s purposes and the particular job or role you hold. That role can change without becoming the whole measure of your purpose.
3. My past sins do not change my call.

“I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who has given me strength, that he considered me trustworthy, appointing me to his service. Even though I was once a blasphemer and a persecutor and a violent man, I was shown mercy because I acted in ignorance and unbelief.”
— 1 Timothy 1:12–13, NIV.

kai: Paul’s past did not stop God from showing him mercy and calling him into service. His example offers reassurance that past sins do not put someone beyond God’s mercy or the possibility of a renewed purpose.
4. God empowers what he calls me to do.
“The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do it.”
— 1 Thessalonians 5:24, NIV.

kai: This follows Paul’s prayer for God to make believers holy. The emphasis is on God’s faithfulness in continuing his work in them, rather than a guarantee that every personal ambition will succeed.
“And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose.”
— Romans 8:28, NIV.

kai: The good God works towards may not always look like the outcome you had in mind. This connects with your earlier reflection on Job: trusting God does not mean expecting a life where everything goes your way.
i kinda liken all of this to shooting an arrow.

It is my job to practise drawing the bow, strengthen my arms, and get used to accounting for wind speed, trajectory, yada yada. i still have to put in the work and aim properly. But once the arrow leaves the bow, i cannot keep steering it. There is only so much i can control, and that is where trusting God comes in.
That does not mean every shot will hit the bullseye i had in mind. It means doing my part faithfully and trusting him with the outcome, even when it looks different from what i hoped for.
idk if that makes sense, but i guess the main point is to trust God’s plan for you (and me), and have faith in his timing while continuing to do what is within our control.
i guess i ended up covering both my weekly wrap-up and my religion takes LOL. i am such a yapper fr, but yeah, 🤙🏼 journaling is p fun.
